quests.instruction: Arrange the three things Priya did, in the order she did them.
quests.story: Priya reached the bus stop at 7:30. Her brother had already left on the earlier bus. When the next bus came, she climbed on. Ten minutes later she got off at her school gate.
options: Priya's brother left on the earlier bus.
Priya got off at her school gate.
Priya reached the bus stop at 7:30.
Priya climbed onto the next bus.
quests.hint: Ask who each sentence is about before you start ordering.
quests.explanation: The brother's bus left before Priya even arrived, and it was his journey, not hers. Priya's own steps run from reaching the stop, to boarding the next bus, to getting off at school.
storyKeyEvents: Priya reached the bus stop at 7:30.
Priya climbed onto the next bus.
Priya got off at her school gate.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three things that happened from nine o'clock on.

options: Deng opened his laptop at nine.
Deng charged his laptop the night before.
Deng typed his name and began his essay.
The laptop turned on right away.
quests.hint: Look for a sentence that belongs to a time before the story's starting point.
quests.explanation: Charging the laptop happened the night before nine o'clock, so it is background rather than part of the morning. From nine on, he opens it, it starts, and he begins writing.
storyKeyEvents: Deng opened his laptop at nine.
The laptop turned on right away.
Deng typed his name and began his essay.

Lucia bought a kilo of oranges.
Lucia went to the market for oranges.
Lucia bought two bags and carried them home.
quests.hint: A plan and an event are not the same thing. Check what the story says she did in the end.
quests.explanation: The kilo was only Lucia's plan, and the small bags stopped it from happening. The real sequence is going to the market, finding only small bags, and buying two of them.
storyKeyEvents: Lucia went to the market for oranges.
Lucia found that the seller only had small bags.
Lucia bought two bags and carried them home.

Omar mailed his package.

Omar waited in the line.
Omar mailed his package.

quests.instruction: Arrange only what had already happened by the end of Tuesday.

The receptionist booked Hana's next visit.
Hana came back for another check-up in June.

quests.explanation: The June appointment was only scheduled on Tuesday; it had not taken place. What had happened was the visit, the cleaning and check, and the booking of the next one.
storyKeyEvents: Hana went to the dentist on Tuesday.
The dentist cleaned Hana's teeth and checked for cavities.
The receptionist booked Hana's next visit.

Tomás bought two tickets.

storyKeyEvents: Tomás met his cousin outside the cinema.
Tomás bought two tickets.
Tomás and his cousin found seats before the lights went down.

quests.instruction: Arrange what really happened to Nadia's phone.

Nadia repaired the screen herself with an online kit.
Nadia left the phone at the shop on Monday.
Nadia cracked her phone screen on Saturday.

quests.explanation: The kit was her first idea, dropped after her friend mentioned the shop. The phone actually went from cracked, to the shop on Monday, to collected the same evening.
storyKeyEvents: Nadia cracked her phone screen on Saturday.
Nadia left the phone at the shop on Monday.
Nadia collected the phone that evening.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three steps the students carried out.

options: The students dropped an ice cube into a bowl of warm water.
The students wrote down the minute it disappeared.
Mr. Osei numbered the bowls.
The students watched the ice cube shrink.

quests.explanation: Numbering the bowls was the teacher's preparation, finished before class began. The students' own steps are dropping the ice in, watching it shrink, and recording when it vanished.
storyKeyEvents: The students dropped an ice cube into a bowl of warm water.
The students watched the ice cube shrink.
The students wrote down the minute it disappeared.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three events that make up Wei's morning at the food bank.

Wei sorted the donated bread into crates.
Every crate was labelled by noon.

quests.explanation: Mrs. Diaz's counting was a separate job going on elsewhere in the building. Wei's morning is arriving, sorting the bread, and having everything labelled by noon.
storyKeyEvents: Wei arrived at the food bank at nine.
Wei sorted the donated bread into crates.
Every crate was labelled by noon.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three things that had happened by the time the train reached Ibrahim's stop.

options: Ibrahim collected his bag when the conductor called his stop.
Ibrahim boarded the 8:15 train and found a window seat.
Ibrahim read his book for most of the ride.
Ibrahim's aunt greeted him on the platform.
quests.hint: Check the wording of the last sentence. Is it describing something done or something expected?
quests.explanation: "Would be waiting" describes what was expected at the station, and the story stops before he gets there. The events already finished are boarding, reading, and gathering his bag.
storyKeyEvents: Ibrahim boarded the 8:15 train and found a window seat.
Ibrahim read his book for most of the ride.
Ibrahim collected his bag when the conductor called his stop.

quests.instruction: Choose the three laundry steps and put them in order.

options: Carla carried her laundry to the launderette and started a wash.
Carla moved the clothes to a dryer.
Carla folded the clothes an hour later.
Carla scrolled through her phone while the machine ran.

storyKeyEvents: Carla carried her laundry to the launderette and started a wash.
Carla moved the clothes to a dryer.
Carla folded the clothes an hour later.

quests.instruction: Arrange what actually happened at Jamal's practice.

The players finished with a short game.

storyKeyEvents: The coach moved everyone into the gym.
The players ran passing drills.
The players finished with a short game.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three events in the order they happened.
quests.story: Mira wanted to visit the science museum on her day off. At the entrance she learned that tickets were half price after two o'clock, so she went for a coffee and came back later. She paid for one ticket and walked into the main hall.
options: Mira paid the full ticket price at the entrance.
Mira went for a coffee and came back later.
Mira paid for one ticket and walked into the main hall.
Mira learned that tickets were half price after two o'clock.

quests.explanation: The half-price offer is the reason Mira left and returned, so she never paid full price at the desk. She learned about the offer, waited over a coffee, then bought her ticket.
storyKeyEvents: Mira learned that tickets were half price after two o'clock.
Mira went for a coffee and came back later.
Mira paid for one ticket and walked into the main hall.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three things Ben did to the shelf.
quests.story: Ben's shelf had started to lean. On Saturday he took the books off, then tightened the loose screws. His roommate Luca sanded a rough edge nearby. When the shelf stood straight, Ben put the books back.
options: Ben put the books back.
Ben tightened the loose screws.

Ben took the books off the shelf.
quests.hint: Both roommates are working on the shelf. Sort the actions by who does them.
quests.explanation: Sanding was Luca's contribution, even though it helped the same shelf. Ben's own sequence is emptying the shelf, tightening it, and refilling it.
storyKeyEvents: Ben took the books off the shelf.
Ben tightened the loose screws.
Ben put the books back.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three events that happened on Tuesday.

options: Everyone was back online by four o'clock.
The Wi-Fi went down in the middle of a class.
The router was moved to a shelf by the window.
Mr. Adeyemi restarted the router.
quests.hint: The story opens with a sentence about an earlier day. Be careful about where it sits in time, not just in the text.
quests.explanation: The router was moved earlier in the week, so it can't be one of Tuesday's events even though it is mentioned first. Tuesday itself runs from the outage to the restart to everyone reconnecting.
storyKeyEvents: The Wi-Fi went down in the middle of a class.
Mr. Adeyemi restarted the router.
Everyone was back online by four o'clock.

quests.instruction: Arrange the three events that led to Rosa getting her parcel.

Rosa phoned the depot.
Rosa collected the parcel at the counter the next morning.

Rosa collected the parcel at the counter the next morning.

quests.instruction: Arrange only what the story actually tells us happened.

storyKeyEvents: The card reader stopped working during the lunch rush.
The owner taped a sign asking for cash.
A technician fixed the reader by two o'clock.

Elena drove her sister to the train station on Monday.
